blocks.text: FloppyData in 2026: what you get

FloppyData sells proxies the way prepaid phone plans sell minutes: one flat $1/GB balance that works across residential, mobile and datacenter pools. Static residential IPs start at $1.79 each in monthly bundles (20 for $49) with unlimited bandwidth. It is one of the cheapest ways into residential traffic, but it is a newer brand with less independent benchmarking than the established names.

Strengths: Flat $1/GB on any volume; One balance across residential, mobile and datacenter; Cheap static residential bundles with unlimited bandwidth; Free cloud anti-detect browser. Weak spots: Newer brand with limited independent testing; Pool-size claims disputed by some reviewers; Mixed customer-support reviews.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap has sold proxies since 2018 and says it serves 45,000+ customers. It offers seven product types: static residential (ISP) in IPv4 and IPv6, rotating residential, datacenter IPv4 and IPv6, and static and rotating mobile. Rotating residential is pure pay-as-you-go with no monthly plan, and the site claims coverage in 180+ countries. Targeting is mainly country and ISP level, and all products support SOCKS5 including UDP. It is a strong value pick, though independent benchmarks of its rotating pool have been mixed.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: FloppyData vs Proxy-Cheap

FloppyData charges a flat $1/GB for rotating traffic, and the same balance works for residential, mobile and datacenter IPs. Static residential proxies are sold in monthly bundles from $1.79 per IP (20 IPs for $49), and static datacenter IPs from $0.79 per IP.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

Buying 10 GB, you would pay about $7.80 with Proxy-Cheap and $10 with FloppyData: a 22% saving in Proxy-Cheap's favour. At 100 GB a month, Proxy-Cheap is the cheaper option at about $78 against $100 for FloppyData, roughly 22% less. Both FloppyData and Proxy-Cheap work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

FloppyData and Proxy-Cheap do not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. FloppyData lists '65M+ claimed (disputed)' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, FloppyData lists 148 (residential) countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, FloppyData offers country and city, while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, FloppyData offers rotating or sticky sessions, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With FloppyData: cheap, but with limited independent benchmarking. With Proxy-Cheap: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed. Run the same small test on both before committing.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. FloppyData: workable for light tasks. Proxy-Cheap: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. FloppyData: cheap static residential IPs and a free anti-detect browser. Proxy-Cheap: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities. Let price and the countries you need decide.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. FloppyData: city targeting at a flat rate. Proxy-Cheap: fine for country-level price checks. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Ad verification and geo-testing: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. FloppyData: limited targeting depth and published data. Proxy-Cheap: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Tight budgets: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With FloppyData: a flat $1/GB on any volume. With Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. FloppyData: No free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. FloppyData: Light. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test FloppyData and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle FloppyData vs Proxy-Cheap faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (FloppyData: no free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, FloppyData comes out ahead in 0, Proxy-Cheap in 0, and 6 are ties. With no overall winner, decide on the factor that matters most to you: FloppyData is strongest for small budgets and experiments, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
